turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I know your schedule is brutal.
Okay. Then answer the question, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
I have to say, you're far more reasonable than I expected. Most parents come in swinging.
Don't manage me, Hale. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero, or whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
It's refreshing. You clearly see the whole picture, so I think we're really on the same side here.
Then why are we here? I'm not on a side, Hale, I'm waiting for an answer: who decided on the zero, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
